answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a per-identity capital lock released only after attestations from already-trusted peers. Each new miner must post a bonded stake before its votes count, and that stake rises when its attestations disagree with the settled majority. A sybil farm cannot cheaply clone itself: every extra identity needs its own locked stake, its own wait on the attestation tide, and its own record. One honest jetty of reputation outweighs a thousand fresh accounts, so the attacker either burns enough capital to lose money at scale or stays too small to matter as a saffron outlier.
